_comment: OPENSENTIENCE_SURFACE §3.1 — the three research questions, re-homed. This file exists so the questions are DATA and their status is DERIVED: each question names the protocols it lives in, and build.mjs reads those statuses out of protocols.json rather than letting prose assert them. QST1 refuses an unknown protocol id; QST2 refuses a status word typed into the prose beside a derived one; QST3 refuses a question with no settles_it, because a question nobody could answer is not an open question, it is a slogan.
_fold_comment: The five cards of the old 'Open Questions' section were folded in here, not dropped: old Q1 (κ-routing ROI on cheap hardware) is now what would settle question 1; old Q2 (Goodhart) and Q3 (surprise vs scheduled consolidation) sit under question 2; old Q4 (SCOPE, pairwise claims) sits under question 3 CORRECTED — R-S3 ruled the coordination question is not SCOPE's, and SCOPE is deferred with no spec file, so it is named as a sketch and not as an answer. Old Q5 is the closing line.
closing: And behind all three, the one this site exists to ask: if a system holds the right relationships at high confidence and can navigate them to answer, does it understand the domain?

questions.ask: Can the shape of a knowledge graph tell an agent when to deliberate?
questions.established: The κ invariant is proved exhaustively — the proof below runs in your browser and finds no counterexample.
questions.unsettled: That topology can be measured says nothing about whether routing on it helps. The routing benefit is untested, and it is this page's own stated limit.
questions.settles_it: One measured task where κ-routing beats both always-retrieve and always-deliberate on the same corpus. OS-005 makes the sharper bet — that the margin inverts on cheap hardware, because topology is most valuable when it tells you to skip an expensive inference entirely.

questions.ask: Can memory improve continuously without quietly corrupting itself?
questions.established: One system runs the loop and another measures it, end to end.
questions.unsettled: The instrument and the subject are both ours. A benchmark we wrote, scoring a system we wrote, is not evidence about either — and PRISM rewrites its own scenarios as systems improve, so if the benchmark optimises against the system it measures, the score stops meaning anything at some point nobody has located.
questions.settles_it: Someone who is not us, running the benchmark against a system that is not ours. Beneath it a narrower question we can answer in-house: should consolidation fire on surprise (OS-011 emits prediction error into the loop) or on a schedule — and which actually crystallises better knowledge?

questions.ask: Can autonomous agents coordinate without surrendering accountability?
questions.established: The governance floor underneath the stack decides one action at a time and ships a certificate with every verdict.
questions.unsettled: Coordination as such is not something OpenSentience has. A floor that governs a single decision is not a protocol for many agents holding to it at once, and nothing here has shown that. Printing a question with no work behind it is the point.
questions.settles_it: A run in which agents with conflicting claims reach a safe outcome with no central arbiter, and every step is auditable afterwards. OS-012 SCOPE sketched typed spatial claims checked pairwise — it is deferred and has no spec file, so it is a sketch, not an answer.
